description:
Follow a migration request with the request_id and status_token helpcenter_request_migration returned. Needs no agent_key.

Returns (also as structuredContent): status — queued, in_progress, with_our_team, completed or declined; the request stays open, and its help centers refuse agent-key writes, until every help center is completed or declined; expected_by; retry_after (seconds worth waiting before the next check); help_centers [{site_id, subdomain, status, articles_migrated, claimed, reason, dashboard_url}]; handoff_url, the one claim link while any of its help centers can still be claimed; next_step {code, instruction, url}, the user's next step in words to pass on as they are.

Check at most every retry_after seconds (900): a request answers 60 checks an hour. A wrong id or token answers not found, exactly like a request that does not exist. The token works until 30 days after the request ends.

Args:
  - request_id (number, required)
  - status_token (string, required)
  - response_format ('markdown' | 'json'): default 'markdown'.

response_format.description: Output format: 'markdown' for a human-readable summary or 'json' for the full structured payload.

status_token.description: The status_token helpcenter_request_migration returned with that request: a read-only token for this request alone, not an agent key. Never shown again, so keep it; never show it to the user.

name: helpcenter_get_migration_request
title: Follow a Migration Request
